key_insight: Nominally cubic CsGeBr3 hosts long-lived, one-dimensional polar chains despite having zero net polarization, while its ferroelectric phase reverses polarization chain by chain.
engineering_relevance: These slow, chain-mediated polarization dynamics could inform models of switching and response times in halide-perovskite ferroelectric devices.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials.
Analysis of Ge off-centering, polar correlations, and relaxation dynamics.
Comparison with BaTiO3, PbTiO3, and CsSnBr3.
evidence_signal: Simulations show polar chains extending at least tens of nanometers and relaxing on nanosecond timescales—four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 intermediate.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based findings; experimental confirmation and device-scale switching performance remain unestablished.
paper_title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
